title: Prosthetic Restoration of teeth following proximal box elevation using all-ceramic crowns
summary:
This aim of this study is to evaluate the long-term clinical performance of proximal box elevation as a treatment option for teeth with extensive hard-tissue defects extending below the gingival margin. 
The procedure involves initially elevating the subgingivally located defect to a more accessible level using a tooth-colored restorative material, followed by definitive restoration of the tooth with an all-ceramic crown.
Following crown-placement, the restorations will be clinically evaluated over a 5-year follow-up period.
conditions: Prosthetic Restoration of Teeth with Deep Subgingival Hard-Tissue Defects

interventions.name:
Intervention: Deep margin elevation followed by definitive restoration with an all-ceramic crown
Control: None
Outcome: Long-term clinical survival and success

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults aged ≥18 years who are capable of providing informed consent:
- permanent premolars or molars requiring full-crown restoration with an proximal, subgingival defect, posing a risk of violation of the biological width if restored with a crown according to statutory health insurance guidelines
- a minimum distance of 1.5 mm between the alveolar crest and the proximal box floor/floor of the cavity
- vital teeth without symptoms or teeth with an adequate root canal filling
- a maximum of two teeth per participant
Exclusion criteria:
- inadequate oral hygiene
- para- or subcrestal dental defects affecting the potential study tooth
- inability to achieve adequate moisture control for placement of the core build-up
- insufficient residual tooth structure for adequate retention 
- tooth fractures
- persistent periapical lesions without signs of healing
- untreated periodontitis
- bruxism
